newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena and unions in provisional deal on jobs, wages.
newsitem.headline: Sabena and unions in provisional deal on jobs, wages.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena and its main unions have reached a provisional deal on future wages and working conditions, the unions said on Thursday.
The agreement provides for the retention in the Sabena group of the catering, technical services, ground and cargo handling functions.
It also involves job guarantees for 7,650 full-time workers until the end of 1998.
The deal is conditional on approval by a majority of staff.

The agreement covers increased staff flexibility and a wage freeze for all staff. It also covers the re-instatement of collective bargaining accords cancelled by Sabena at the end of last year in a bid to break the deadlock on talks about a plan to restore profits.
It also includes measures regarding voluntary early retirement and part time work.
The unions said the agreement involved an equal sacrifice by all levels of staff. Personnel would be given further information in the next few days.

The unions said they assumed that given the current economic and financial shape of Sabena this deal was the best that could be obtained and the best way of guaranteeing future employment of Sabena staff.
The deal is the result of four months of talks between Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by Swissair, and unions.
It is part of the 4.7 billion Belgian franc Horizon 98 plan to boost profitability.
Under the plan, staff is to accept two billion francs worth of job and pay cuts, and increased flexibility, while 2.7 billion francs are to come from cost cuts and revenue increases.
